title: Jungle vs Ret / Arms / Disc
summary: A machine-drafted plan for Feral / BM Hunter / Disc into Ret Paladin, Arms Warrior and Disc Priest. Kill target, control allocation and cadence are derived from cooldowns and DR; the order is a guess. Correct it on any step.

sections.title: Kill the Warrior — and here is the arithmetic, not an opinion
sections.body:
The Paladin holds eight defensive answers, including Divine Shield (5 min), Blessing of Protection (5 min), Blessing of Spellwarding (5 min), Lay on Hands (10 min), Divine Protection (90s), Blessing of Sacrifice (60s) and a trinket. The Warrior holds four: Die by the Sword (2 min), Berserker Shout (60s), Spell Reflection (25s) and a trinket.

So the Warrior's answer pool empties in one go and the Paladin's does not. That is the whole reason for the target call.

What this does NOT account for: how hard each of them is to actually keep in melee range, and whether pressure on the Paladin is worth more as peel-suppression than as damage. Both of those are judgement, not data.

sections.title: Cadence: 30 seconds, with a real go every 90
sections.body:
Almost everything this comp needs sits on the same tier: Freezing Trap 25s, Maim 30s, Psychic Scream 30s, Scatter Shot 30s, Bestial Wrath 30s, Feral Frenzy 30s, Tiger's Fury 30s. Intimidation at 40s and Binding Shot at 45s are the two that drift.

So the comp repeats a full control-plus-damage attempt every 30 seconds, and a big one every 90 when Incarnation returns. Power Infusion at 120s only makes every second big go.

The consequence: spending Maim or the trap off-cycle costs more than the ability itself, because the next attempt arrives with them no longer lined up.

sections.title: Where this is guessing — tell it what a real player does instead
sections.body:
1. The Cyclone. It is the only free control in the comp, and this plan cannot decide whether it belongs on the healer at 50% or on the Paladin at full. Which is right, and does it depend on whether their trinket is up?

2. Incarnation lasts far longer than 5 seconds of Maim. This plan controls the healer through the window instead of the target — is that right, or should control be held back so it is live when Sacrifice ends?

3. Whether the opener should force Sacrifice cheaply and commit on the second go instead. This plan commits on the first one.

4. Nothing here accounts for positioning. Same-global cross-CC on the Paladin assumes he is reachable when the Warrior is.
